verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν
verses.transliteration: Meta de to pausasthai ton thorybon metapempsamenos ho Paulos tous mathētas kai parakalesas aspasamenos exēlthen poreuesthai eis Makedonian
verses.literal: When the uproar had ended Paul sent for the disciples And after encouraging them he said goodbye to them and left for . . . Macedonia
verses.literalPt: E, DEPOIS que cessou o alvoroço, Paulo chamou a si os discípulos e, abraçando-os, saiu para a Macedônia.

verses.original: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα
verses.transliteration: dielthōn de ta merē ekeina kai parakalesas autous logō pollō ēlthen eis tēn Hellada
verses.literal: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement . . . . . . . . . he arrived in Greece
verses.literalPt: E, havendo andado por aquelas terras, exortando-os com muitas palavras, veio à Grécia.

verses.original: ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς γενομένης ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας
verses.transliteration: poiēsas te mēnas treis genomenēs epiboulēs autō hypo tōn Ioudaiōn mellonti anagesthai eis tēn Syrian egeneto gnōmēs tou hypostrephein dia Makedonias
verses.literal: where he stayed three months And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria he decided . . . to go back through Macedonia
verses.literalPt: E, passando ali três meses, e sendo-lhe pelos judeus postas ciladas, como tivesse de navegar para a Síria, determinou voltar pela Macedônia.

verses.original: Συνείπετο δὲ αὐτῷ Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος
verses.transliteration: Syneipeto de autō Sōpatros Pyrrou Beroiaios Thessalonikeōn de Aristarchos kai Sekoundos kai Gaios Derbaios kai Timotheos Asianoi de Tychikos kai Trophimos
verses.literal: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica Gaius from Derbe Timothy and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia
verses.literalPt: E acompanhou-o, até à Ásia, Sópater, de Beréia, e, dos de Tessalônica, Aristarco, e Segundo, e Gaio de Derbe, e Timóteo, e, dos da Ásia, Tíquico e Trófimo.

verses.original: οὗτοι δὲ προελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι
verses.transliteration: houtoi de proelthontes emenon hēmas en Trōadi
verses.literal: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas
verses.literalPt: Estes, indo adiante, nos esperaram em Trôade.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε ὅπου διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά
verses.transliteration: hēmeis de exepleusamen meta tas hēmeras tōn azymōn apo Philippōn kai ēlthomen pros autous eis tēn Trōada achri hēmerōn pente hopou dietripsamen hēmeras hepta
verses.literal: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread we sailed from Philippi and five days later we rejoined them in Troas where we stayed seven days
verses.literalPt: E, depois dos dias dos pães ázimos, navegamos de Filipos, e em cinco dias fomos ter com eles a Trôade, onde estivemos sete dias.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου
verses.transliteration: En de tē mia tōn sabbatōn synēgmenōn hēmōn klasai arton ho Paulos dielegeto autois mellōn exienai tē epaurion pareteinen te ton logon mechri mesonyktiou
verses.literal: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread Since Paul was ready to leave the next day he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight
verses.literalPt: E no primeiro dia da semana, ajuntando-se os discípulos para partir o pão, Paulo, que havia de partir no dia seguinte, falava com eles; e prolongou a prática até à meia-noite.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι
verses.transliteration: Ēsan de lampades hikanai en tō hyperōō hou ēmen synēgmenoi
verses.literal: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered
verses.literalPt: E havia muitas luzes no cenáculo onde estavam juntos.

verses.original: καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός
verses.transliteration: kathezomenos de tis neanias onomati Eutychos epi tēs thyridos katapheromenos hypnō bathei dialegomenou tou Paulou epi pleion katenechtheis apo tou hypnou epesen apo tou tristegou katō kai ērthē nekros
verses.literal: And a certain young man named Eutychus seated in the window was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on When he was sound - asleep he fell . . . from the third story and was picked up dead
verses.literalPt: E, estando um certo jovem, por nome Êutico, assentado numa janela, caiu do terceiro andar, tomado de um sono profundo que lhe sobreveio durante o extenso discurso de Paulo; e foi levantado morto.

verses.original: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: katabas de ho Paulos epepesen autō kai symperilabōn eipen Mē thorybeisthe hē gar psychē autou en autō estin
verses.literal: But Paul went down threw himself on the young man and embraced him Do not be alarmed he said He is still alive . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Paulo, porém, descendo, inclinou-se sobre ele e, abraçando-o, disse: Não vos perturbeis, que a sua alma nele está.

verses.original: Ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφ’ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν
verses.transliteration: Anabas de kai klasas ton arton kai geusamenos eph’ hikanon te homilēsas achri augēs houtōs exēlthen
verses.literal: Then Paul went back upstairs broke bread and ate And after speaking until daybreak he departed
verses.literalPt: E subindo, e partindo o pão, e comendo, ainda lhes falou largamente até à alvorada; e assim partiu.

verses.original: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως
verses.transliteration: ēgagon de ton paida zōnta kai pareklēthēsan ou metriōs
verses.literal: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive
verses.literalPt: E levaram vivo o jovem, e ficaram não pouco consolados.

verses.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ προελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον οὕτως γὰρ διατεταγμένος ἦν μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν
verses.transliteration: Hēmeis de proelthontes epi to ploion anēchthēmen epi tēn Asson ekeithen mellontes analambanein ton Paulon houtōs gar diatetagmenos ēn mellōn autos pezeuein
verses.literal: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos where we were to take Paul aboard He had arranged this because he was going there . . . . . . on foot
verses.literalPt: Nós, porém, subindo ao navio, navegamos até Assôs, onde devíamos receber a Paulo, porque assim o ordenara, indo ele por terra.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην
verses.transliteration: hōs de syneballen hēmin eis tēn Asson analabontes auton ēlthomen eis Mitylēnēn
verses.literal: And when he met us at Assos we took him aboard . . . and went on to Mitylene
verses.literalPt: E, logo que se ajuntou conosco em Assôs, o recebemos, e fomos a Mitilene.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ἄντικρυς Χίου τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς Σάμον τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον
verses.transliteration: kakeithen apopleusantes tē epiousē katēntēsamen antikrys Chiou tē de hetera parebalomen eis Samon tē de echomenē ēlthomen eis Milēton
verses.literal: Sailing on from there we arrived the next day opposite Chios The day after that we arrived at Samos and on the following day we came to Miletus
verses.literalPt: E, navegando dali, chegamos no dia seguinte defronte de Quios, e no outro aportamos a Samos e, ficando em Trogílio, chegamos no dia seguinte a Mileto.

verses.original: Κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα
verses.transliteration: Kekrikei gar ho Paulos parapleusai tēn Epheson hopōs mē genētai autō chronotribēsai en tē Asia espeuden gar ei dynaton eiē autō tēn hēmeran tēs Pentēkostēs genesthai eis Hierosolyma
verses.literal: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid . . . spending time in the province of Asia because he was in a hurry to reach . . . Jerusalem if possible by the day of Pentecost
verses.literalPt: Porque já Paulo tinha determinado passar ao largo de Éfeso, para não gastar tempo na Ásia. Apressava-se, pois, para estar, se lhe fosse possível, em Jerusalém no dia de Pentecostes.

verses.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας
verses.transliteration: Apo de tēs Milētou pempsas eis Epheson metekalesato tous presbyterous tēs ekklēsias
verses.literal: From Miletus Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church
verses.literalPt: E de Mileto mandou a Éfeso, a chamar os anciãos da igreja.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφ’ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθ’ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην
verses.transliteration: Hōs de paregenonto pros auton eipen autois Hymeis epistasthe apo prōtēs hēmeras aph’ hēs epebēn eis tēn Asian pōs meth’ hymōn ton panta chronon egenomēn
verses.literal: When they came to him he said You know how I lived the whole time I was with you from the first day - I arrived in the province of Asia
verses.literalPt: E, logo que chegaram junto dele, disse-lhes: Vós bem sabeis, desde o primeiro dia em que entrei na Ásia, como em todo esse tempo me portei no meio de vós,

verses.original: δουλεύων τῷ Κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων
verses.transliteration: douleuōn tō Kyriō meta pasēs tapeinophrosynēs kai dakryōn kai peirasmōn tōn symbantōn moi en tais epiboulais tōn Ioudaiōn
verses.literal: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears especially in the trials . . . that came upon me through the plots of the Jews
verses.literalPt: Servindo ao Senhor com toda a humildade, e com muitas lágrimas e tentações, que pelas ciladas dos judeus me sobrevieram;

verses.original: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατ’ οἴκους
verses.transliteration: hōs ouden hypesteilamēn tōn sympherontōn tou mē anangeilai hymin kai didaxai hymas dēmosia kai kat’ oikous
verses.literal: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house
verses.literalPt: Como nada, que útil seja, deixei de vos anunciar, e ensinar publicamente e pelas casas,

verses.original: διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν εἰς Θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ πίστιν εἰς τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν
verses.transliteration: diamartyromenos Ioudaiois te kai Hellēsin tēn eis Theon metanoian kai pistin eis ton Kyrion hēmōn Iēsoun Christon
verses.literal: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ
verses.literalPt: Testificando, tanto aos judeus como aos gregos, a conversão a Deus, e a fé em nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo.

verses.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ δεδεμένος ἐγὼ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά μοι μὴ εἰδώς
verses.transliteration: Kai nyn idou dedemenos egō tō pneumati poreuomai eis Ierousalēm ta en autē synantēsonta moi mē eidōs
verses.literal: And now compelled by the Spirit I am going to Jerusalem not knowing what will happen to me there
verses.literalPt: E agora, eis que, ligado eu pelo espírito, vou para Jerusalém, não sabendo o que lá me há de acontecer,

verses.original: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν
verses.transliteration: plēn hoti to Pneuma to Hagion kata polin diamartyretai moi legon hoti desma kai thlipseis me menousin
verses.literal: I only know that in town after town . . . the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me
verses.literalPt: Senão o que o Espírito Santo de cidade em cidade me revela, dizendo que me esperam prisões e tribulações.

verses.original: ἀλλ’ οὐδενὸς λόγου ποιοῦμαι τὴν ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: all’ oudenos logou poioumai tēn psychēn timian emautō hōs teleiōsai ton dromon mou kai tēn diakonian hēn elabon para tou Kyriou Iēsou diamartyrasthai to euangelion tēs charitos tou Theou
verses.literal: But I consider my life of no . . . value to me if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace
verses.literalPt: Mas em nada tenho a minha vida por preciosa, contanto que cumpra com alegria a minha carreira, e o ministério que recebi do Senhor Jesus, para dar testemunho do evangelho da graça de Deus.

verses.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν
verses.transliteration: Kai nyn idou egō oida hoti ouketi opsesthe to prosōpon mou hymeis pantes en hois diēlthon kēryssōn tēn basileian
verses.literal: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again
verses.literalPt: E agora, na verdade, sei que todos vós, por quem passei pregando o reino de Deus, não vereis mais o meu rosto.

verses.original: διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων
verses.transliteration: dioti martyromai hymin en tē sēmeron hēmera hoti katharos eimi apo tou haimatos pantōn
verses.literal: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men
verses.literalPt: Portanto, no dia de hoje, vos protesto que estou limpo do sangue de todos.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: ou gar hypesteilamēn tou mē anangeilai pasan tēn boulēn tou Theou hymin
verses.literal: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God
verses.literalPt: Porque nunca deixei de vos anunciar todo o conselho de Deus.

verses.original: Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου
verses.transliteration: Prosechete heautois kai panti tō poimniō en hō hymas to Pneuma to Hagion etheto episkopous poimainein tēn ekklēsian tou Theou hēn periepoiēsato dia tou haimatos tou idiou
verses.literal: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers Be shepherds of the church of God which He purchased with His own blood
verses.literalPt: Olhai, pois, por vós, e por todo o rebanho sobre que o Espírito Santo vos constituiu bispos, para apascentardes a igreja de Deus, que ele resgatou com seu próprio sangue.

verses.original: ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου
verses.transliteration: egō oida hoti eiseleusontai meta tēn aphixin mou lykoi bareis eis hymas mē pheidomenoi tou poimniou
verses.literal: I know that after my departure savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock
verses.literalPt: Porque eu sei isto que, depois da minha partida, entrarão no meio de vós lobos cruéis, que não pouparão ao rebanho;

verses.original: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ἑαυτῶν
verses.transliteration: kai ex hymōn autōn anastēsontai andres lalountes diestrammena tou apospan tous mathētas opisō heautōn
verses.literal: Even from your own number men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them
verses.literalPt: E que de entre vós mesmos se levantarão homens que falarão coisas perversas, para atraírem os discípulos após si.

verses.original: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον
verses.transliteration: dio grēgoreite mnēmoneuontes hoti trietian nykta kai hēmeran ouk epausamēn meta dakryōn nouthetōn hena hekaston
verses.literal: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears
verses.literalPt: Portanto, vigiai, lembrando-vos de que durante três anos, não cessei, noite e dia, de admoestar com lágrimas a cada um de vós.

verses.original: Καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ὑμᾶς τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ τῷ δυναμένῳ οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai ta nyn paratithemai hymas tō theō kai tō logō tēs charitos autou tō dynamenō oikodomēsai kai dounai tēn klēronomian en tois hēgiasmenois pasin
verses.literal: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified
verses.literalPt: Agora, pois, irmãos, encomendo-vos a Deus e à palavra da sua graça; a ele que é poderoso para vos edificar e dar herança entre todos os santificados.

verses.original: Ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα
verses.transliteration: Argyriou ē chrysiou ē himatismou oudenos epethymēsa
verses.literal: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing
verses.literalPt: De ninguém cobicei a prata, nem o ouro, nem o vestuário.

verses.original: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται
verses.transliteration: autoi ginōskete hoti tais chreiais mou kai tois ousin met’ emou hypēretēsan hai cheires hautai
verses.literal: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions . . . . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Sim, vós mesmos sabeis que para o que me era necessário a mim, e aos que estão comigo, estas mãos me serviram.

verses.original: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν
verses.transliteration: panta hypedeixa hymin hoti houtōs kopiōntas dei antilambanesthai tōn asthenountōn mnēmoneuein te tōn logōn tou Kyriou Iēsou hoti autos eipen Makarion estin mallon didonai ē lambanein
verses.literal: In everything I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself It is more blessed to give than to receive
verses.literalPt: Tenho-vos mostrado em tudo que, trabalhando assim, é necessário auxiliar os enfermos, e recordar as palavras do Senhor Jesus, que disse: Mais bem-aventurada coisa é dar do que receber.

verses.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο
verses.transliteration: Kai tauta eipōn theis ta gonata autou syn pasin autois prosēuxato
verses.literal: When Paul had said this he knelt down . . . . . . . . . with all of them and prayed
verses.literalPt: E, havendo dito isto, pôs-se de joelhos, e orou com todos eles.

verses.original: ἱκανὸς δὲ κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο πάντων καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: hikanos de klauthmos egeneto pantōn kai epipesontes epi ton trachēlon tou Paulou katephiloun auton
verses.literal: They all wept openly as they embraced . . . . . . . . . . . . Paul and kissed him
verses.literalPt: E levantou-se um grande pranto entre todos e, lançando-se ao pescoço de Paulo, o beijavam,

verses.original: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον
verses.transliteration: odynōmenoi malista epi tō logō hō eirēkei hoti ouketi mellousin to prosōpon autou theōrein proepempon de auton eis to ploion
verses.literal: They were especially grieved . . . by his statement that they would never see his face again Then they accompanied him to the ship
verses.literalPt: Entristecendo-se muito, principalmente pela palavra que dissera, que não veriam mais o seu rosto. E acompanharam-no até o navio.
